pr_title: feat(page): Pick best locator for existing element.
pr_body:
Improve programmatic API of accessing the "pick locator" functionality as exposed by the playwright trace viewer/codegenerator.

Fixes #13900


I am not sure if this is the both the best way to implement it (sorry in advance, first time contributing here) nor the best API, so would love some feedback on both.

Overall: it would be super helpful for us (octomind) to programmatically be able to pick the "best" locator/selector for a certain HTMLElement we have in-memory already. Our use-case is a little different than the one referenced in the issue: we want to be able to auto-generate playwright tests using some form of AI/smart exploration. To do that effectively we would like to be able to choose the "best" selector/locator for a certain element that we already hold in-memory from our exploration process so that the resulting test case is as robust as possible. 

If you need more information we can go also go into more detail. We in general would love to help give playwright a programmatic API if allowed , e.g. test execution and introspection of test results is something we are very interested in as well (see https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/7275).

Re: this specific change: I was looking to build an API that works on a certain HTMLElement directly, but found it a) difficult to get that through the serialization between client/server and b) thought that a selector -> "better" selector API might be more generic anyways.
pr_comments: Closing as per above, please feel free to open a new issue if this does not cover your use case.

Hi @pavelfeldman @mxschmitt sorry for the late reply, just as a fyi:

unfortunately the solution as provided by max does not seem to work in headless mode, it requires setting PWDEBUG=console which will launch the browser WITH ui. It's somewhat okay for us, but does require quite a bit of workarounds to make it work in a server-/serverless environment.

issue_context.title: [Feature] SelectorGenerator as standalone package
issue_context.body:
Hi,
The selector-generator component which is injected as part of the codegen mode has significant utility outside of playwright.
I'd really like to use it stand-alone. I think there's a lot of projects which would like to also.

Would you consider publishing this independely, or providing a code-sample which uses just this alone?

Thanks!
comments: @samdoeswork Tell us more about your usecase? Where do you intend to use it? We don't have plans to provide a standalone package right now, but more details will help us prioritize it.

Thanks @dgozman 

The selector-generator is so elegant. My use-case is somewhat niche: detecting when elements appear during manual browser-sessions.

For my case, I want to use your brilliant selector-generation engine to generate data on what a user does in browser.
The goal (for me) isn't to record and replay, it's to record and use that data.

- Imagine editing tutorial videos & having precise timestamps on when you did various actions so you can very easily edit the video, and/or automatically provide chapter markers to the user.
- Imagine automatic record-keeping for timesheet-bound employees or highly regulated industries

For my particular use case I want to automatically timestamp media, by correlating in-browser elements of interest with the time in the recording -- making these elements searchable, jump-to, bulk edit, etc.

There's a very long tail of times where it's useful to identify moments when you did something.

I realize it's niche compared to record & replay.

Another obvious use-case is de-coupling the record & replay: people may need to lightly customize one part or both.


There are quite a few automation use-cases which open up if you can - for example - select an element in browser and say "send a webhook whenever this shows up" or "send a screenshot whenever this shows up" or even "inject code whenever this shows up". This opens the door for semi-automation features; people removing a few clicks from their repetitive work, etc.

@samdoeswork These are interesting ideas, but seem to be out of scope for Playwright, at least right now. That said, I'll keep the issue open just in case. Meanwhile, feel free to fork/copy the selector generator, it is open source after all 😄

review_comments: How does using a selector which depends on the content of the website such as name of buttons, placeholders be more stable than id, data-testid etc.?

well, ids are often changing, in some frameworks even for each reload.

data-testids are of course the most stable, but in our use case (see [octomind](www.octomind.dev)) we don't control the actual source of the website we're testing and don't want our customer to have to make changes.

also, but not a very strong argument over testids, if accesibility is of concern to you it of course helps to see if people are breaking the accessible aria-labels etc. if you use them in your tests.
